html:
The Emirate of Sicily was the Muslim state on the island of Sicily from the 800s to the 1000s. It is on the map for 900 and 1000.

Sicily had been a Byzantine province. In 827 an army of the Aghlabids of Tunisia landed at Mazara and began a slow conquest that took most of a century: Palermo fell in 831, Syracuse in 878 and Taormina in 902. Sicily then passed to the Fatimids, who from 948 left it to emirs of the Kalbid family.

Palermo, called Balarm, became one of the great cities of the Mediterranean, with many mosques and markets. The Arabs spread irrigation and new crops, such as lemons, oranges, sugar cane and cotton. In the 1000s the emirate split into rival lords. The Norman Roger I invaded in 1061 and finished the conquest in 1091. Arab learning lived on at the Norman court, where al-Idrisi made his world map, and in Sicily long after.
sum: The Emirate of Sicily was the Muslim state on the island of Sicily from the 800s to the 1000s. It is on the map for 900 and 1000.
